notes: Four university-layer documents (instructor announcement, committee report, Fall 2026 teaching guidance, TLL ChatGPT page); all four coded stance delegates by both coders. Alignment was by position in the saved text (overlapping or adjacent anchors) with manual repair of a few pairs (committee-report A64/B40 version-history, A154/B95 distinguish-own-work, A43/B25 collaborative spaces; TLL case-by-case and under-18 sentences). Main disagreement kinds: (1) granularity: coder A split lists into separate units (B.2 permitted uses, assessment-design options, prohibited uses, privacy facts, faculty-support items, survey findings) and found 86 more passages than B, mostly rationale/evidence sentences; all were checked against the text and kept as real policy statements, while the one A unit that duplicated a B recommendation (collaborative spaces) was folded into B's should-unit; (2) phase: whether posting/communicating a policy is before-course or course-start (resolved: course-start for posting, before-course for design choices) and design versus during-work for assignment-structuring options (resolved: before-course); (3) modality: informs versus should/must for descriptive or consequence sentences (resolved by whether the sentence directs someone: duties and recommendations got must/should, descriptions got informs); (4) policy_type: tool-for-instructors (P63 over P04), process-evidence (P40 over P26), instructor AI use (P47/P59), lockdown browsers (P22), tier-fit statements (P05 over P33/P09), UNCOVERED items re-mapped where a type clearly fit (case-by-case equity note to P51, enforcement caveat to P01); (5) unit_stance: coder B used permit/encourage/restrict for disclosure and design sentences; resolved to neutral unless the sentence itself limits or invites AI use. Three UNCOVERED units remain in the committee report (assessment-reliability claim, bypassing human learning settings, instructor referral of students to support). No new types.
